Subject: Post-demo: POC capacity plan & traffic acceptance matrix

Hi Sofia — great demo today, thanks for the time. 

Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the POC intake and acceptance gates. Please flag anything we got wrong.

High-level success criteria (customer & Redwood alignment):
- Functional: the PoC must demonstrate accurate intent and response quality across your top-10 intents (we'll use the sample prompts you shared).
- Performance: for the targeted flows, 95% of inference requests should complete end-to-end under 300 ms p50 and p90 < 600 ms for the evaluated workload on Redwood Dedicated capacity.
- Throughput & stability: sustain 50 RPS steady-state; tolerate burst windows up to 200 RPS for 20–30s without request drops.
- Cost guardrail: tokenized unit economics should be within the threshold you indicated (goal: <$0.0015 per generated token for the POC profile).
- Ops: no more than 2 incidents requiring manual intervention during the 3-week evaluation window.

POC logistics (proposed):
- Evaluation window: 3 weeks (candidate start: 2026-11-30 through 2026-12-20).
- Owners: Rishi (Sales / program lead), Ben (Infra owner for capacity and kernel tuning), Marissa (Customer success / acceptance signoff).
- Deliverables: workload ingestion spec, synthetic load script, side-by-side latency / cost dashboard, final acceptance report.

Traffic intake (what we need from Acme to size the run):
- Steady RPS target: 50 RPS (per earlier call).
- Burst profile: up to 200 RPS for 20–30s, expected twice per day during business hours.
- Concurrency: ~120 concurrent user sessions (chat-style session affinity).
- Typical prompt lengths: 30–60 input tokens (median ~40).
- Typical response lengths: 100–200 tokens (median ~150).
- Token distribution: 60% short (<=80 tokens), 30% medium (81–250), 10% long (>250).
- Endpoints: /chat (primary), /summarize (occasional heavy payloads), /embed (background embeddings at lower QPS).

Attachments included: acme_poc_traffic_profile.xlsx (template), sample_prompts_v1.txt (your examples).

Next steps (action items):
1) Sofia / Acme: confirm acceptance of criteria above and share any additional traffic logs (if available) + procurement contact.
2) Acme: return completed traffic_profile.xlsx by 2026-11-24.
3) Ben / Infra: prepare a Dedicated capacity quote and initial config by 2026-11-26.
4) Rishi / Marissa: schedule a 30-min kickoff the week of 2026-11-30 if dates align.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the MSA and a one-page mutual action plan.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Technical intake: POC traffic profile & config proposal

Folks — attaching a filled example of the traffic_profile spreadsheet plus a short config proposal. Key technical takeaways and assumptions below.

Assumptions pulled from Rishi / Sofia thread:
- Model variant for POC: rwd-midi-8b-q4 (balance of latency and quality per our catalog).
- Average tokenization: median input 40 tokens, median output 150 tokens. We used your distribution percentages to generate synthetic traces.
- Workload mix: 78% /chat, 12% /summarize, 10% /embed.

Sizing proposal (initial):
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs with continuous provisioning for 50 RPS. Autoscale policy to add 2 GPUs during sustained >70 RPS and a hard burst buffer to handle transient 250 RPS for 10s without queuing.
- KV cache: session cache with retention 30 min, approx 14GB total KV footprint estimated from median session lengths.
- Batching and token budgets: dynamic batching window set to 12 ms; max batch size tuned for target p50 latency.

Acceptance test plan (tech):
1) Synthetic run: reproduce 1-hour steady-state at 50 RPS + 2 planned bursts (200–250 RPS) and measure p50/p90/p99 latency and tail error rates.
2) Real-data sanity: run a 2-hour ingestion of redacted real queries from Acme and validate quality delta vs baseline (human spot checks + automated intent accuracy).
3) Cost reconciliation: capture tokens / GPU-hours during runs and compare to expected token-unit budget.

I've attached: acme_poc_traffic_profile.xlsx (sample filled), and a short runbook snippet embedded in the spreadsheet.

If this looks good I’ll schedule a technical kickoff with Daniel to walk through the synthetic trace and runbook on 2026-11-29.

—Ben
